history.period: Modern (Sindhi community temple); founding date undocumented
history.summary: A Sindhi community temple in Junagadh city dedicated to Jhulelal, the patron water deity (ishta-dev) of the Sindhis. A place listing gives its address as 1, Adarsh Nagar Main Rd, Junagadh (21.528215, 70.448879), with daily hours 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM (verify). Its founding date and history are undocumented online - many such Gujarat Jhulelal temples were established by Sindhi migrants after Partition, but this is UNVERIFIED for this shrine. Distinct from the Jay Jhulelal Temple at Bantwa, Junagadh district (~35 km away). media is empty: no reliable image of the Junagadh mandir was found after searching.

name: Jhulelal Mandir, Junagadh
town_description: Junagadh is a city at the foot of the Girnar hills in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, once the capital of the former princely state of Junagadh. It is known for the Ashokan rock edicts (c. 250 BCE), the Uparkot fort and the Mahabat Maqbara, and is the gateway for pilgrims climbing Mount Girnar and visitors to Sasan Gir. The district headquarters is a major religious-tourism hub of western Gujarat.

travel.road: Adarsh Nagar Main Rd, Junagadh city; accessible by local transport

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Cheti Chand (March-April) is the main festival
